Eukaryotyping ensemble distance

Source: R/eukaryotyping.R
euk_ensemble_distance.Rd

Combines the heuristic and Bayesian distance matrices into a single ensemble. Two rules are available: `"original"` (default) reproduces the distribution-mapping procedure of the original `run.r` script shipped with Barratt et al. (2019); `"rank"` is a package-specific direction-consistent fractional-rank mean.

Usage

euk_ensemble_distance(
  geno,
  ploidy,
  ids = NULL,
  method = c("original", "rank"),
  seed = NULL,
  epsilon = 0.3072,
  ...
)

Arguments

geno

List of `n x maxMOI` integer matrices (one per locus).

ploidy

Integer vector (1 = haploid, 2 = diploid) for each locus.

ids

Optional character vector of sample identifiers.

method

Combination rule. `"original"` (default) reproduces the combining procedure of the original `run.r` script: the Bayesian matrix is reversed (`2 - D_bayesian`), both matrices are min-max normalised over all entries including the diagonal, the sorted Bayesian values are mapped onto the ranks of the heuristic matrix, the ensemble is the elementwise mean of the mapped and heuristic matrices, rescaled by its maximum. Random tie breaking makes this method non-deterministic without `seed` and can yield a non-symmetric matrix. `"rank"` is a package-specific fractional-rank mean over the strictly upper triangle, with the Bayesian matrix reversed so both components are divergence-oriented; its diagonal is `NA`.

seed

Optional integer seed for the `"original"` method's random tie breaking. Ignored for `method = "rank"`.

epsilon

Rate of missed alleles for the Bayesian component.

...

Passed to [euk_heuristic_distance()] (e.g. `m`, `impute_data`, `use_r`).

Value

An `n x n` matrix of ensemble distances (in \([0, 1]\) for `method = "rank"` off-diagonal entries). Larger values indicate pairs that both components rank as more divergent.
